o1.biggest_strength: It builds the whole series around the two behaviors most tied to retention, uses only triggers the tool actually supports, and cleanly branches by signup platform.
o1.biggest_mistake: Email 5 repeats the recurring-task push instead of testing whether a later, segmented Pro message might be better for engaged users.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep this structure, then tighten Email 5 by either segmenting it further or briefly justifying why a second recurring-task push beats a delayed Pro message for this onboarding window.

o2.biggest_strength: The writing sounds on-brand and the platform-based second-device email is strong and useful.
o2.biggest_mistake: It keeps a Pro email in the 5-email onboarding series and gives up the fifth slot that could have pushed one of the two retention-driving habits again.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the Pro email with another habit-building email tied to recurring tasks or second-device use, and make the success metrics center more clearly on both-habits adoption and day-30 retention.

reason: Output 1 is more focused on what our data says actually drives retention, and it is closer to something I would ship without edits. Output 2 is good, but it spends a valuable onboarding slot on Pro before fully maximizing the habit-building opportunity.
